Annotated step outputs

Source: R/pipeflow.R
pip_output_value.Rd

pip_output_value() is an extension point for annotating the outputs of a pipeline, for example to stamp a result with the step it came from or the time it was computed. It can be thought of as a hook that allows you to postprocess or annotate the output of a step before it is stored. The generic is applied to the output of a step right after the step function returns, and its result is what is stored as the step's output.

Usage

pip_output_value(x, ctx = list(), ...)

Arguments

x

The output value of a step, or one of its partitions if the output is partitioned.

ctx

Named list describing the context of the value:

  • step: the name of the step, as it was before the step ran.

  • key: the partition key, or NULL if the output is not partitioned.

  • time: the time stamp of the step's run, which is the same for all partition keys and is also stored as the step's time.

...

Currently unused, reserved for future extensions. Methods should accept it.

Value

The value that is stored as the step's output.

Details

The default method returns x unchanged. Methods are meant for your own classes, not for base classes such as numeric or character.

The generic is applied once to the output as a whole, so a method sees the whole object a step returned. The one exception is a partitioned output (a step with exec = "split", or a step that was mapped over a partitioned input): there the generic is applied once per partition, and each partition gets its key in ctx$key.

If you want to annotate an output element-wise instead of the whole object, just write a method that walks over each element. For example, for a plain list, a method could look something like this:

pip_output_value.list <- function(x, ctx = list(), ...) {
    x[] <- lapply(x, FUN = pip_output_value, ctx = ctx)
    x
}

The generic is not applied to the outputs of failed steps (see pip_run(on_error = "continue")), which remain the condition of the failure, nor to the inputs a step receives from other steps: it acts on what a step returns, once. An error in a method is an error of the step and is handled like any other step error; for a partitioned output it names the partition key the method failed for.

See also

pip_param_value(), pip_run()

Examples

# Stamp every output with the step it came from
stamped <- function(x) structure(x, class = "stamped")

pip_output_value.stamped <- function(x, ctx = list(), ...) {
    attr(x, "step") <- ctx[["step"]]
    x
}
registerS3method("pip_output_value", "stamped", pip_output_value.stamped)

p <- pip_new() |>
    pip_add("make", \(n = 3) stamped(seq_len(n)))
pip_run(p, lgr = NULL)
attr(p[["make", "out"]], "step")
#> [1] "make"
